Research

Rocky exoplanet interiors and atmospheres

Observation-constrained theoretical modelling

Planetary bulk composition plays a key role in determining planetary interiors, which in turn exert first-order control on surface and atmospheric evolution.

Publications

  • The compositional link between rocky exoplanets and their host stars is consistent with Earth-like devolatilization
    Y. Reinarz, L. Acuña-Aguirre, H. S. Wang (2026)
    Astronomy & Astrophysics, accepted; arXiv:2611.12581 · arXiv
    Interior structure retrievals of 14 rocky exoplanets with two independent models find that 8 present an Earth-like devolatilization trend relative to their host stars, while only one shows a 1:1 relationship between planetary and stellar abundances.
  • Thermal Evolution of Lava Planets Across System Ages: Predictions for Hell of a Survey
    M. Sastre, T. Lichtenberg, L. Dang, A. Piette, H. S. Wang, M. López-Morales, et al. (2026)
    arXiv:2609.20155 · arXiv
    Coupled interior–atmosphere models of the five lava-planet targets of JWST Cycle 4 program 8864 predict that most tend toward a bare-rock end-member, with atmospheric retention sensitive to escape efficiency.
  • The Barnard’s Star planetary system: stability, composition, and evolution of four sub-Earth exoplanets
    X. Byrne, C. M. Guimond, A. Bonsor, H. S. Wang, S. R. Vaughan, J. G. Rogers (2026)
    Monthly Notices of the Royal Astronomical Society, 550, stag1207 · DOI · arXiv
    The high Mg/Si and low Th/Mg ratios of Barnard’s Star imply that its four sub-Earth planets have ferropericlase-rich mantles with about half of Earth’s radiogenic heating, and are unlikely to have outgassed secondary atmospheres.
  • Origin and characterization of super-Earths and sub-Neptunes
    L. Parc, J. Venturini, F. Bouchy, R. Helled, C. Dorn, A. Leleu, Y. Alibert, S. Müller, H. Wang (2026)
    The NCCR PlanetS Legacy Book; arXiv:2604.11779 · arXiv
    Reviews the detection, characterization and theoretical interpretation of super-Earths and sub-Neptunes within NCCR PlanetS over 2014–2025.
  • ExoInt: Devolatilization and interior modeling package for rocky planets
    H. S. Wang (2022–2026)
    Astrophysics Source Code Library, ascl:2504.019 · Link
    Open-access package that models the interior structure and mineralogy of rocky planets from devolatilized stellar compositions.
  • The PLATO mission
    H. Rauer, C. Aerts, J. Cabrera, et al. (incl. H. S. Wang) (2025)
    Experimental Astronomy, 59, 26 · arXiv
    Overview of ESA’s PLATO mission, which will detect and characterise small planets around bright stars, including terrestrial planets in the habitable zone of solar-like stars.
  • Plausible constraints on the range of bulk terrestrial exoplanet compositions in the solar neighbourhood
    R. J. Spaargaren, H. S. Wang, S. J. Mojzsis, M. D. Ballmer, P. J. Tackley (2023)
    The Astrophysical Journal, 948, 53 · DOI · arXiv
    Devolatilized stellar abundances from the Hypatia and GALAH catalogues constrain the range of rocky exoplanet compositions in the solar neighbourhood, with metallic core sizes varying from 18 to 35 wt%.
  • A model Earth-sized planet in the habitable zone of α Centauri A/B
    H. S. Wang, C. H. Lineweaver, S. P. Quanz, S. J. Mojzsis, T. R. Ireland, P. A. Sossi, F. Seidler, T. Morel (2022)
    The Astrophysical Journal, 927, 134 · DOI · arXiv
    Predicts the bulk composition, interior structure and early atmosphere of a hypothetical Earth-sized planet in the habitable zone of the nearest binary system.
  • Detailed chemical compositions of planet-hosting stars II: exploration of the interiors of terrestrial-type exoplanets
    H. S. Wang, S. P. Quanz, D. Yong, F. Liu, F. Seidler, L. Acuña, S. J. Mojzsis (2022)
    Monthly Notices of the Royal Astronomical Society, 513, 5829–5846 · DOI · arXiv
    Models of hypothetical habitable-zone terrestrial planets around 13 planet-hosting Sun-like stars suggest that most have broadly Earth-like composition and interior structure, with those of Kepler-10 and Kepler-37 as strongly oxidised exceptions.
  • Europium as a lodestar: diagnosis of radiogenic heat production in terrestrial exoplanets
    H. S. Wang, T. Morel, S. P. Quanz, S. J. Mojzsis (2020)
    Astronomy & Astrophysics, 644, A19 · DOI · arXiv
    Proposes europium as a practical proxy for radiogenic heating in exoplanetary systems, and finds a lower radiogenic heat budget for a model Earth-like planet around α Centauri A/B than for Earth.
  • Enhanced constraints on the interior composition and structure of terrestrial exoplanets
    H. S. Wang, F. Liu, T. R. Ireland, R. Brasser, D. Yong, C. H. Lineweaver (2019)
    Monthly Notices of the Royal Astronomical Society, 482, 2222–2233 · DOI · arXiv
    Shows that devolatilized stellar abundances reduce the degeneracy of exoplanet interior inference relative to mass–radius data alone. Introduced ExoInt.
